title: How the pieces move: an overview
line: All six pieces, one board each. The lessons after it take each piece up close.

steps.text: A piece moves to an empty square, or captures an enemy piece by moving onto its square. The captured piece leaves the board.
The rook moves in straight lines, as far as the way is clear. Tap every square this rook can reach.
steps.after: It stops before its own pawn, and it can capture the knight.

steps.text: The bishop moves along diagonals, as far as the way is clear. Tap every square this bishop can reach.
steps.after: A bishop stays on squares of one color all game.

steps.text: The queen moves like a rook and a bishop together. Tap every square this queen can reach.
steps.after: Her own pieces block every other line for now.

steps.text: The knight jumps two squares one way and one square to the side. Tap every square this knight can reach.
steps.after: The knight is the only piece that can jump over others.

steps.text: The king moves one square in any direction. Tap every square this king can reach.
steps.after: The king may never move onto a square where it could be captured.

steps.text: A pawn moves straight ahead, one square, or two on its first move. Tap every square the pawn on e2 can reach.
A pawn captures one square diagonally forward. Tap every square the pawn on e4 can reach.
steps.after: It can step one square forward, or capture the pawn diagonally.

summary: Rooks go straight, bishops go diagonally, the queen does both. Knights jump, kings step, pawns push.
